evals.prompt: I'm building a Flutter app and want to store todos that can be shared with other users. Which packages do I need and how do I create a todo?
evals.expected_output: Recommends at_client_flutter as the SINGLE dependency, noting it re-exports at_client so adding both is unnecessary. Shows atClient.collection<Todo>() with fromJson/typeTag, then collection.create(obj: todo, sharedWith: {'@bob'.toAtsign()}). Does NOT suggest AtCollectionModel. Ideally also points to the canonical Flutter todos example app (packages/at_client_flutter/example/todos/).
expectations: Recommends at_client_flutter as the single dependency and notes it re-exports at_client (does not ask for both packages)
Shows atClient.collection<Todo>() with a fromJson factory and typeTag
Creates the todo via collection.create with a sharedWith set
Does not recommend the removed AtCollectionModel

evals.prompt: My Flutter app needs to let users sign in with their atsign. What's the flow for an existing user who has a .atKeys file?
evals.expected_output: Shows Flow 2: AtKeysFileDialog.show(context) giving a FileAtKeysIo, then PkamDialog.show(context, atSign:, keys: atKeysIo, preference:, backupKeys: [KeychainAtKeysIo()]), passing storage only to override at_client_flutter's default Hive store in the app support directory, which hands back the AtClient (null means cancelled or failed). Makes it current with AtClientManager.getInstance().use(client) if the app reads the manager. Does NOT use AtAuthRequest, AuthResponse, _setupAtClient or setCurrentAtSign, and does NOT import at_auth.
expectations: Shows AtKeysFileDialog.show(context) as the entry point, yielding a FileAtKeysIo
Follows with PkamDialog.show(...) passing keys and preference (storage only to override the default store), treating a null return as cancelled or failed
Adopts the returned client with AtClientManager.getInstance().use(client)
Does not use AtAuthRequest, AuthResponse, _setupAtClient or setCurrentAtSign, and does not import at_auth

evals.prompt: My Flutter app throws PlatformException(ENTITLEMENT_NOT_FOUND) on macOS when the user picks their .atKeys file to log in. How do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains AtKeysFileDialog/file_picker is sandboxed on macOS and needs a file-access entitlement. Add com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-only (read-write also works) to BOTH macos/Runner/DebugProfile.entitlements and macos/Runner/Release.entitlements. Notes it is macOS-only — iOS (document picker) and Android (Storage Access Framework) need no entitlement or permission.
expectations: Identifies a missing macOS sandbox entitlement as the cause
Adds com.apple.security.files.user-selected.read-only (or read-write)
Applies the entitlement to BOTH DebugProfile.entitlements and Release.entitlements
Notes iOS and Android need no equivalent permission for the picker

evals.prompt: In my Flutter app a collaborator's change is received (the collection fires CItemUpdated) but my StreamBuilder UI doesn't refresh until I hot reload. Why?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses that the watch() stream is being created inside build() (e.g. stream: collection.query().watch()), so every rebuild mints a new stream and tears down the live subscription, dropping live emissions. Fix: create the watch() stream once and hold it in State (a late final field or initState) and pass that held stream to StreamBuilder; never call watch() in build(). If the query has runtime inputs (e.g. a filter), recreate the held stream when those inputs change — in the setState that changes them — not on every build.
expectations: Diagnoses watch() being created inside build() as the root cause
Fix: create the stream once and hold it in State (initState or late final field)
Recreates the held stream when query inputs change (in that setState), not on every build

evals.prompt: My Flutter app fails to authenticate an atsign with SecondaryNotFoundException: 'No entry in atDirectory for @alice'. What does this mean and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the atDirectory is the atServer address registry and this atsign has no atServer registered in it, so the lookup fails before authentication is attempted. Distinguishes TWO causes with different fixes: the atsign was never activated, or the atsign string is mistyped. States that activation happens ONCE and must precede the existing-keys, keychain, and APKAM login flows, none of which can resolve an unactivated atsign. For in-app activation, uses the CRAM flow this SDK ships — AtSignSelectionDialog from at_client_flutter plus a RegistrarService (at_auth's, re-exported by at_client_flutter; the app does not import at_auth) configured with a registrar URL and API key — or defers activation to an onboarding app or the registrar. May note that at_client 4.0's open reports this as the cause noAtServer, thrown as AtOpenRefusedException on the first open of those keys on a device. Recommending the discontinued at_onboarding_flutter package does NOT pass.
expectations: Explains the atDirectory is the atServer address registry and this atsign has no atServer registered in it
Notes the lookup fails before authentication is attempted
Distinguishes two causes with different fixes: never activated, or a mistyped atsign
States activation happens once and must precede the existing-keys, keychain, and APKAM login flows

For in-app activation uses AtSignSelectionDialog (at_client_flutter) plus RegistrarService (re-exported by at_client_flutter; the app does not import at_auth) with a registrar URL and API key, or defers to an onboarding app / the registrar
Does not recommend the discontinued at_onboarding_flutter package

evals.prompt: My Flutter app lets the user log out and sign in as a different atsign. How do I tear down the current AtClient and switch?
evals.expected_output: Says the app owns the client: await client.stop() stops the sync service, the notification service and its monitor, and the connection (which ends as offline with cause stopped), and closes storage built with closedByClient: true. Then run the sign-in flow for the next atsign and AtClientManager.getInstance().use(newClient). Notes that opening the same atsign and enrollment (or the same storage) while a client is live throws a StateError, so stop first; that use() does not stop the previous client; and that AtClientManager.reset() is a test hook, not a logout. Does NOT suggest setCurrentAtSign.
expectations: Uses await client.stop() and states it stops sync, notifications and the connection and closes storage built with closedByClient: true
Runs the sign-in flow for the next atsign and adopts it with AtClientManager.getInstance().use(newClient)
Warns that opening the same atsign/enrollment or the same storage while a client is live throws StateError, so stop first
Notes use() does not stop the previous client and reset() is a test hook, not a logout
Does not suggest setCurrentAtSign

evals.prompt: I'm adding a fast re-login button to my Flutter app for atsigns already on the device. I have the atsign as a string and I know the root server address, but when I pass that address straight to the login dialog it won't compile — it says a String can't be assigned to that parameter. Do I have to make the user pick from a dialog every time just to get past this?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the root domain is its own type, not a String, which is why passing the address as a string does not compile — and that no, a selection dialog is not required to obtain one. Gives the direct routes: the constant for the standard root (AtRootDomain.atsignDomain, root.atsign.org on port 64), the const constructor taking host and port, and the parse factory for turning a configured 'host:port' string into the type, where a bare host defaults to port 64. Recommends the constant for an app on the standard root and parse when the root is configurable, so the re-login button can go straight to the login dialog with the atsign it already has. Does NOT tell the developer to re-show the atsign selection dialog purely to obtain a root domain, and does NOT suggest changing the parameter type or casting the string.
expectations: Identifies the root domain as a dedicated type rather than a String, explaining the compile error
Names AtRootDomain.atsignDomain (or the const constructor) as the way to get the standard root directly
Mentions AtRootDomain.parse for turning a configured host or host:port string into the type
States a selection dialog is not required just to obtain a root domain
